snippet.title: 5 API Performance Tips Every Backend Developer Should Know ⚡ | Caching, Compression & Pagination
snippet.description:
5 API Performance Tips Every Backend Developer Should Know  | Caching, Compression & Pagination

Want to build faster and more scalable APIs? In this short video, you'll learn 5 powerful API performance optimization techniques that every backend developer should know.

In this video:
    Caching – Reduce database load and dramatically lower latency.
    Connection Pooling – Reuse database connections for better throughput.
    Async Logging – Prevent logging from slowing down your requests.
    Compression (Gzip/Brotli) – Reduce response size by up to 70%.
    Pagination – Return smaller, predictable result sets.

These techniques are essential for developers working with:
    PHP and Laravel
    Node.js and Express.js
    Django and FastAPI
    Spring Boot
    REST APIs and microservices

If you're building high-performance backend systems, these API optimization strategies will help you improve speed, reduce server load, and scale efficiently.

snippet.description:
AI is changing quickly, but the most valuable professionals will be the ones who know how to adapt, experiment, and apply the right tools with judgment.

snippet.title: IFRS vs US GAAP – Major Differences Simplified (LIFO, Development Cost, Revaluation)
snippet.description:
What is the difference between IFRS and U.S. GAAP?

In this video, we clearly explain the key differences between International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) in a simple and practical way.

We cover:

✔ Principles-based vs Rules-based approach
✔ LIFO inventory method differences

snippet.title: The Audit Breakthrough with Copilot by Chris Stegh | Miles Masterclass Trailer
snippet.description:
Microsoft Copilot is changing how audit teams plan, document, test, communicate, and manage engagements, but auditor judgment remains at the center.

In this Miles Masterclass course, The Audit Breakthrough with Copilot, Chris Stegh demonstrates how Microsoft Copilot can support a complete modern audit engagement from risk assessment through final audit committee communication.

Across the course, learners follow the fictional audit of Brightline Retail Corp. while exploring how AI-powered workflows can improve audit planning, journal entry testing, walkthrough documentation, PBC management, substantive testing, memo drafting, client communication, and governance reporting.

The course shows how Copilot works inside the tools auditors already use, including Excel, Word, Teams, Outlook, and PowerPoint. Rather than treating AI as a separate tool, Chris explains how audit teams can use Copilot to analyze large data sets, surface anomalies, organize documentation, draft communications, and create clearer reporting.

Learners will also explore practical audit use cases such as risk-ranked analytics, fraud-focused journal entry testing, walkthrough narratives, PBC tracking, revenue and receivables testing, going concern evaluations, management letters, and audit committee presentations.

The course also introduces the CARE framework, covering Context, Action, Results, and Exception Handling, to help professionals prompt, review, and refine AI-assisted outputs responsibly while maintaining human oversight and accountability.

Watch the full course to learn how audit teams can use Microsoft Copilot to reduce administrative friction, improve engagement coordination, strengthen documentation, and focus more time on the critical thinking that drives audit quality.
